title: Problem 1.3
statement_text: What is the infimum of fractional chromatic numbers of planar graphs without cycles of length 4 or 5?
context_text: For positive integers $b\le a$, an $(a:b)$-coloring of $G$ assigns to each vertex a $b$-element subset of $\{1,\dots,a\}$ so that adjacent vertices receive disjoint subsets (an $(a:1)$-coloring is a proper $a$-coloring); the fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ is the infimum of $a/b$ over all $(a:b)$-colorings of $G$, and $\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G)$. Steinberg's conjecture, that every planar graph without cycles of length 4 or 5 is 3-colorable, was disproved by Cohen-Addad et al.; it is natural to ask for a constant $c<4$ with $\chi_f(G)\le c$ for all such graphs. The authors prove that every planar graph without cycles of length 4 or 5 is $(11:3)$-colorable, hence has $\chi_f\le\frac{11}{3}$ and independence ratio at least $\frac{3}{11}$. The question asks for the optimal such constant; the paper writes "infimum", but given the discussion it means the best possible upper bound $c$, i.e. the supremum of $\chi_f(G)$ over planar graphs without cycles of length 4 or 5. The authors suspect $\frac{11}{3}$ is not optimal, and remark that the counterexample to Steinberg's conjecture is $(6:2)$-colorable, so they cannot even exclude that the answer is $3$.
paper_title: Planar graphs without cycles of length 4 or 5 are (11:3)-colorable

title: Informal conjecture on optimality of 11/3
statement_text: It is not clear whether the constant $\frac{11}{3}$ in the bound $\chi_f(G)\le\frac{11}{3}$ for every planar graph $G$ without cycles of length 4 or 5 is the best possible, and we suspect this is not the case.
